anti_patterns.name: text parsing for loop control
anti_patterns.explanation: checking literal words like 'done' or 'finished' to exit loop, claude might say 'done' in step 1 but theres still a lot of steps, always use stop_reason

anti_patterns.name: fixed iteration cap as primary control
anti_patterns.explanation: primary exit must always be stop_reason == end_turn

anti_patterns.name: keyword detection for tool routing
anti_patterns.explanation: read the structured tool_use blocks in the content array, dont check if claudes text mentions a tools name to decide what to call

things_to_know: loop pattern
tools are descriptions
stop_reason is the only control signal
messages array grow every iteration
model-driven means claude what to do next (claude is planner)
tool results go back as user role messages, wrapped in tool_result block with the matching id
use while true with safety counter as fallback, never fixed range as primary exit condition

anti_patterns.name: direct subagent-to-subagent communication
anti_patterns.explanation: subagents never message each other

anti_patterns.name: assuming inherited context
anti_patterns.explanation: subagents start fresh

anti_patterns.name: always-on full pipeline
anti_patterns.explanation: triggering all subagents on every request regardless of complexity (dynamic routing)

anti_patterns.name: overly narrow decomposition
anti_patterns.explanation: splitting tasks so finely that subagents have overlapping scopes

anti_patterns.name: raw text handoffs
anti_patterns.explanation: passing unstructured text between agents with no source attribution (source, url, date)

things_to_know: hub-and-spoke - coordinator and subagents
isolated context - subagents start fresh
responsibilities - decompose -> delegate -> aggregate -> evaluate -> respond
task tool - spawns subagents; coordinators allowed_tools must include "Task"
parallel execution - multiple task calls
sequential execution - one task per loop iteration
dynamic routing - only invoke subagents needed for request
structured harndoffs - every response from subagents need to be structured
iterative refinement - coordinator evaluates results, re-delegates if needed

anti_patterns.name: forgetting "Task" in allowed_tools
anti_patterns.explanation: cant spawn subagents

anti_patterns.name: giving all tools too all agents
dumping entire conversation history into task prompt
procedural prompts that specify every step
anti_patterns.explanation: let claude decide execution path

anti_patterns.name: unstructured data handoffs
anti_patterns.explanation: raw text blobs with no metadata - always include source, date, confidence

anti_patterns.name: treating parallel vs sequential as a style preference

things_to_know: Task tool creates isolated subagents - "Task" MUST be in coordinators allowed_tools
AgentDefinition has 5 fields - name, description, system_prompt, tools, allowed_tools
Minimum-tools principle - each agent only gets tools needed for the job
Subagents start black - pass all needed context: facts, constraints, format, prior results
sequential = await chain - parallel = asyncio.gather()
Fork = multiple subagents from same baseline, each exploring different direction
specify goals + output format - never specify exact tool call sequences
Structured metadata in all handoffs - source, date, confidence score for every cross-agent data transfer

anti_patterns.name: "dont run payment without validation" as prompt, trusting claude will follow it. Correct way is to use code gate that blocks payment_tool, until validate_card_tool passes
Claude calls tools out of oder
anti_patterns.explanation: it thinks skipping a step is efficient. Correct way is to enforce order with prerequisite gate checks

anti_patterns.name: escalating with "i need help"
anti_patterns.explanation: human has no context to act. Correct way is using structured handoff - action_requested, context, options, recommended_action

anti_patterns.name: registering hooks but ignoring their return values. Always propagate hook decisions
anti_patterns.explanation: if a hook block, the tool must not run

anti_patterns.name: decomposing depended concerns in parallel
anti_patterns.explanation: agents that share state or need each others output. Only parallelize truly independent investigations

things_to_know: probabilistic = claudes judgement (prompts), deterministic = your code (enforcement)
safety-critical constraints MUST be code-enforced
prerequisite gates block downstream tools until prerequisites succeed
irreversibility test - if a mistake cannot be undone -> code enforcement is required
structured escalation handoffs - always include action_requested, context, options, recommended_action
PreToolUse can block, modify, allow. PostToolUse can validate, transform, record
Multi-concert decomposition - parallelize independent concerns only, if concern B need A's output - use sequential

anti_patterns.name: relying on prompts for data consistency
anti_patterns.explanation: claude misinterprets unix timestamps, use hooks

anti_patterns.name: blocking calls with no explanation
anti_patterns.explanation: claude retries endlessly, always return clear message and alternative action

anti_patterns.name: silently modifying data in hooks
anti_patterns.explanation: debugging becomes impossible, always log all transformations and keep originals

anti_patterns.name: using hooks for soft preferences
anti_patterns.explanation: adds latency, reserve them for hard rules only

anti_patterns.name: no redirect on blocked calls
anti_patterns.explanation: claude will get stuck, always provide alternative - escalation, different tool, human handoff

things_to_know: PostToolUse hooks normalize data into consistent formats
PreToolUse hooks block policy-violating calls
hooks are deterministic, prompts are probabilistic (1-5% failure)
always explain why call was blocked
normalization targets - unix to iso, numeric to string statuses, regional to standard dates
keep hooks fast - they run on every tool call, no network calls
"guarantee compliance" answer is always hooks, not prompts

anti_patterns.name: all files, one prompt
anti_patterns.explanation: attention dilution trap, always decompose into profile passes

anti_patterns.name: using dynamic decomposition for predictable tasks
overly narrow subtask definitions
anti_patterns.explanation: coordinator tasked with researching "create industries" decomposes it only into visual arts subtasks, something like fils or music is missed. Subtasks must cover the full scope

anti_patterns.name: no cross-file integration pass
anti_patterns.explanation: always add a cross-cutting integration pass

things_to_know: prompt chaining - fixed sequential pipeline, use for predictable repeatable tasks
dynamic decomposition - adaptive plan, use for open ended investigation where scope is unknown
split large reviews into per-file passes plus a separate cross-file integration pass
attention dilution - LLMs pay less attention for content thats not in beginning or end of context
adaptive plans add, remove, reorder steps based on findings
chaining is cheaper, dynamic decomposition costs more

anti_patterns.name: resuming code when files were heavily modified
anti_patterns.explanation: you should start fresh or tell claude explicitly what changed

anti_patterns.name: starting fresh when context is still valid
anti_patterns.explanation: resume instead

anti_patterns.name: never using named sessions
anti_patterns.explanation: you lose all progress when terminal is closed

anti_patterns.name: forking for simple linear tasks
anti_patterns.explanation: only use forks when comparing alternatives in parallel

anti_patterns.name: resuming with exhausted context
anti_patterns.explanation: start fresh with injected concise summary of key findings

things_to_know: --resume - resumes named session with full conversation history
stale context is biggest risk of resumption
mitigation 1: inform the resumed session about specific changes
mitigation 2: start a fresh session and inject a structured summary of prior key findings
fork_session - creates session branches from shared analysis baseline, use this to compare strategies in parallel
start fresh when code changed significancy, context is exhausted, or taking new direction
session management is all about preserving valuable analysis while avoiding stale context

anti_patterns.name: minimal descriptions
anti_patterns.explanation: tool descriptions should include purpose, inputs, outputs, when to use

anti_patterns.name: overlapping descriptions
anti_patterns.explanation: each tool must have unique description, otherwise claude can pick any of such tools

anti_patterns.name: system prompt keyword collisions
anti_patterns.explanation: tool names should not match system prompt words

anti_patterns.name: missing boundary conditions
anti_patterns.explanation: state when not to use the tool, example - not for PDFs

things_to_know: tool description is the primary mechanism how claude chooses the tool
five primary elements for tool description - purpose, input format, output, when to use, when not to use
split generic tools to specific tools
renaming ambiguous tools - dont chose generic names
system prompt keywords can make claude pick tools just by keyword matches
when exam shows misrouting problem - improve the description first

parts.topic: structured error responses for mcp tool

anti_patterns.name: generic errors
anti_patterns.explanation: include errorCategory, isRetryable, suggestion

anti_patterns.name: returning empty results for failures
anti_patterns.explanation: an empty array tells the user that nothing exists when in reality it was timeout error

anti_patterns.name: retrying business rule violations
anti_patterns.explanation: set business rule violations as isRetryable: false

anti_patterns.name: propagate all errors to the coordinator
anti_patterns.explanation: handle transient errors locally in subagents

anti_patterns.name: no partial results in error reports
anti_patterns.explanation: always include what was attempted and alternatives exist

things_to_know: 4 error categories - transient, validation, business, permission
5 structure error fields - errorCategory, isRetryable, message, customerMessage, suggestion
access failures vs empty results
local recovery for subagent transient errors
isRetryable: false on business violations prevent wasted max_tokens
escalation reports - always include partial results and alternatives in escalation reports

anti_patterns.name: every agent gets all tools
anti_patterns.explanation: maximizes decision complexity

anti_patterns.name: 18 tools per agent
anti_patterns.explanation: reliability drops when agent has more than 4-5 tools

anti_patterns.name: no cross-role tools at all
anti_patterns.explanation: forces expensive roundtrip with the coordinator for simple operations

anti_patterns.name: auto for output
anti_patterns.explanation: using "auto" when structured output is required, claude may return text. Use "any" to guarantee a tool call

anti_patterns.name: generic tools
anti_patterns.explanation: broad tools like fetch_url, replace them with alternatives with limited scope

things_to_know: too many tools degrade reliability, aim for 4-5 tools per subagent
scoped access - each subagent only gets the tools they need for their role
cross-role tools are the exception, they are for high-frequence operations that would otherwise require roundrips with coordinator
tool_choice - auto (claude decides), any (must call any tool), forced (must call specific tool)
forced tool selection ensures a specific tool runs first, used for ordered pipelines
replace generic tools with constrained alternatives that limit scope (fetch_url vs load_document)

anti_patterns.name: hardcoded secrets in .mcp.json
anti_patterns.explanation: use ${token}

anti_patterns.name: buildint custom servers for standard integrations
anti_patterns.explanation: use community servers

anti_patterns.name: no resources for content catalogs
anti_patterns.explanation: agents will keep repeatedly explore tool calls to discover whats available. Expose issue sumaries, schemas, categories as resources

anti_patterns.name: shared config at user level
anti_patterns.explanation: for team based configs they need to be in project root, not ~/.claude.json

anti_patterns.name: minimal mcp tool description
anti_patterns.explanation: fix the description by modifying CLAUDE.md, not the mcp itself

things_to_know: shared vs user level configs - .mcp.json - commited, ~/.claude.json - user stored
${token} - keep actual keys out of config files
claude discovers all mcp tools simultaneously at connection
mcp resources are read-only catalogs - issue summaries, database schemas, documentation outlines
build custom mcp servers when no community ones exist
enhance mcp descriptions by modifying CLAUDE.md, not mcp directly

anti_patterns.name: reading all files upfront
anti_patterns.explanation: this fills context window with irrelevent files, start with grep to find entry points, then read selectivly

anti_patterns.name: using grep to find file names
anti_patterns.explanation: use glob

anti_patterns.name: using write to modify one line
anti_patterns.explanation: use edit for small changes

anti_patterns.name: using edit on non-unique match
anti_patterns.explanation: include more surrounding context or fallback to read + write strategy

anti_patterns.name: using bash for file search
anti_patterns.explanation: built in grep and glob are more optimal

things_to_know: grep searches file contents, glob searches file names and paths
search strategy - grep first, then read
edit for targeted changes require unique match, write for new files or complete rewrides
edit fails on non-unique match - use fallback - read + write
incremental exploration - follow imports and functions calls step by step - dont read entire codebase
bash is for build, test, install, git - not for filesearch, use built in grep and glob tools

anti_patterns.name: massive monolithic claude.md file
anti_patterns.explanation: split it with imports or rules

anti_patterns.name: team conventions at user level config
anti_patterns.explanation: other team members wont get them, put them at project-level

anti_patterns.name: personal prefs at project-level
anti_patterns.explanation: personal preferences belong in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md - not commited

anti_patterns.name: no modular organization
anti_patterns.explanation: use imports or rules

anti_patterns.name: not checking /memory when claude ignores rules
anti_patterns.explanation: verify that claude sees the config

things_to_know: three config levels - user, project, subdirectory
priority tiers - subdirectory > project > user
add @import external md files to keep claude.md small and readable
.claude/rules/ - directory holds rules and no imports needed, this is loaded automatically
split monolithic claude.md files to small file with imports/rules
use /memory to verify that claude is loading your rules
team member missing conventions - check if config is at user-level instead of project-level

anti_patterns.name: team commands at user level
anti_patterns.explanation: know personal vs project level

anti_patterns.name: skills without fork context
anti_patterns.explanation: verbose output will fill the main conversation, use isolated sub-agent with fork

anti_patterns.name: skills for full tool access for read only tasks
anti_patterns.explanation: use allowed-tools to restrict/protect from executing unwanted tools

anti_patterns.name: universal sdandard as skill
anti_patterns.explanation: if something needs to be run always - use claude.md, if something needs to be run sometimes - use skills

anti_patterns.name: user skills with same name as project skills
anti_patterns.explanation: project level will override user level - use different name to avoid this collision

things_to_know: commands - user vs project scope
skills support with yaml formatter, context:fork, allowed-tools, argument-hint
content: fork - isolates skill in sub-agent
allowed-tools - restricts tool access
skills are on-demand, claude.md always loaded - universal standards stay in claude.md, tasks worflows go in skills
personal skill variants must have different name to avoid overriding team skills

anti_patterns.name: using subdirectory claude.md for cross-cutting concerns
anti_patterns.explanation: its inefficient to put claude.md files in every directory - use path specific rules

anti_patterns.name: no paths field in rules file
anti_patterns.explanation: without path field rules always loaded, use path to scope the rule

anti_patterns.name: overly broad glob patterns
anti_patterns.explanation: be specifc

anti_patterns.name: relying on claude to infer which section applies
anti_patterns.explanation: use paths

things_to_know: .claude/rules/ files with a path enable conditional convention loading
glob patterns control when rules load
path-specific rules beat subdirectory claude.md for cross-cutting concerns (tests spread everywhere, would need to create a lot of claude.md files)
token saving - only load relevant conventions by narrowing path scope
maintaining conventions for files spread across many directories - use path-specific rules, not subdirectory claude.md files

parts.topic: when to use plan mode vs direct execution

anti_patterns.name: using direct execution on architectural change
anti_patterns.explanation: use plan mode

anti_patterns.name: using plan mode on a single file bufxi
anti_patterns.explanation: unnecessary overahead, scope is already clear

anti_patterns.name: starting over when complexity is found
anti_patterns.explanation: start with plan mode when complexity is suspected

anti_patterns.name: plan mode without reviewing the plan
anti_patterns.explanation: the checkpoint is the whole point of plan mode, review it before committing

anti_patterns.name: skipoping explore subagent
anti_patterns.explanation: main context fills with verbose output from discovery, use explore agent to isolate investigation output

things_to_know: plan mode - architectural changes, multi-files changes, multiple approaches, migrations
direct execution - single file changes, simple bug fixes, known approaches
explore subagent runs in isolation when investigating, only clean output returns back to main context
combine both modes, first plan, then review, then execute
when exam describes monolith-to-microservice or a large migration - use plan mode, adding a simple validation - direct execution
plan modes value is in the human review checkpoint - always review the plan and adjust if needed

anti_patterns.name: only using descriptions
anti_patterns.explanation: provide 2-3 concrete input/output examples

anti_patterns.name: implementing without tests
anti_patterns.explanation: write tests first, then iterate using failures

anti_patterns.name: fixing interacting issues one at the time
anti_patterns.explanation: address interacting issues in one pass

anti_patterns.name: skipping interview pattern in unknown codebases
anti_patterns.explanation: ask claude to interview you

anti_patterns.name: vague error reports
anti_patterns.explanation: share tests failures with expected results

things_to_know: concrete input/output examples are more effective than prose descriptions
test-driven iteration - write tests first, run, then iterate failures until pass
interview pattern - tell claude ask questions before committing in unfamiliar domains
interacting issues - must be fixed in one message
specific tests cases - most efficient way to handle edge cases

anti_patterns.name: running claude -p in ci/cd
anti_patterns.explanation: without the -p flag it runs as interactive session, doesnt exit

anti_patterns.name: reviewing code in same session where the code was written
anti_patterns.explanation: claude will be biased, likely wont catch issues

anti_patterns.name: no prior findings in re-reviews
anti_patterns.explanation: include prior findings, report only new issues

anti_patterns.name: no CLAUDE.md for CI context
anti_patterns.explanation: document review criteria in CLAUDE.md

anti_patterns.name: text output in CI
anti_patterns.explanation: use --output-format json

anti_patterns.name: not providing existing tests while generating new ones
anti_patterns.explanation: include existing test files in context

things_to_know: -p flag runs claude non interactively
--output-format json - produces structured json response
claude.md provide consistent context for both interactive and non interactive sessions
session isolation - always review in new session
include prior findings to re-reviews to prevent duplicates
include existing tests when generating new ones to avoid duplicate coverage

anti_patterns.name: "be conservative"
anti_patterns.explanation: this is subjective and it lets claude decide - define explicit categories of what to report

anti_patterns.name: "only high-confidence findings"
anti_patterns.explanation: again lets claude decide what is high-confidence - list specific issue types with code examples

anti_patterns.name: reporting all possible issues
anti_patterns.explanation: define what to skip as explicitly what to report

anti_patterns.name: keeping high false positives categories
anti_patterns.explanation: disable the, improve criteria, re-enable later

anti_patterns.name: no severity examples
anti_patterns.explanation: provide code examples for each severity level

things_to_know: explicit criteria outperform vague descriptions every time
categorical definitions (list of issue types) work better than subjective thresholds
concrete code examples for each severity level
define what to skip as explicitly as what to report
high false positive rates destroy trust across all categories - disable problematic categories and improve them before re-enabling

anti_patterns.name: not including edge case examples
anti_patterns.explanation: always include at least one edge case and null example

anti_patterns.name: examples without reasoning
anti_patterns.explanation: always include why each action was choosing

anti_patterns.name: too many examples (10+)
anti_patterns.explanation: wasted tokens, 2-4 is enough

anti_patterns.name: examples that all look the same
anti_patterns.explanation: claude doesnt learn how to differentiate, make examples structurally diverse

anti_patterns.name: relying on instructions for format
anti_patterns.explanation: show exact output format in examples

things_to_know: few-shot examples are the most effective technique for consistent output when instructions alone produce inconsistent results
include reasoning - "why this action" - so claude learns the pattern
show edge cases and ambiguous scenarios - this is where few-shot examples add the most value
null and missing field handling - must be demonstrated via examples
2-4 examples is the sweet spot - cover common cases, edge cases, format
few-shot examples enable generalization to novel patterns

parts.topic: structured output patterns (why asking for json output in a prompt is unreliable)
things_to_know: tool_use with json schemas eliminates syntax errors (api enforces valid json at system level)
tool_choice: "any" - guarantees claude calls a tool instead of returning text
nullable fields prevent hallucination - make fields optional
enum with "unclear" and "other" prevents forced misclassification of ambiguous cases
forced tool selection ensures a specific extract tool runs first when you know the document type
tool use eliminates syntax errors but not semantic errors (values of json can still be wrong)

anti_patterns.name: retrying when data is absent from the source
anti_patterns.explanation: the correct approach is check if data is not missing, if it is just return null

anti_patterns.name: retrying without specific errors
anti_patterns.explanation: always include previous errors when retrying

anti_patterns.name: no detected_pattern field
anti_patterns.explanation: without this tag, cant analyze false positive trends

anti_patterns.name: only checking structural validity
anti_patterns.explanation: misses the semantic errors

anti_patterns.name: unlimited retries
anti_patterns.explanation: max 1-2 retries

anti_patterns.name: not knowing when to retry
anti_patterns.explanation: retrying when data is missing vs retrying when data was missed or misformatted

things_to_know: retry-with-error-feedback - include original document, failed extraction, specific errors in the retry prompt
retries only work for structured errors or mismatched format, not for information absence from the source
self-correction - extract stated_total and calculated_total, flag conflicts with conflict_detected boolean
semantic validation (totals match, dates format consistent) is separate from schema validation (json valid)

anti_patterns.name: using batch api for blocking workflows
anti_patterns.explanation: for real time use synchronous api

anti_patterns.name: resubmiting the entire batch on partial failure
anti_patterns.explanation: resubmit only the failures by using custom_id

anti_patterns.name: no prompt refining before large batch
anti_patterns.explanation: test on a sample set first with synchronous api

anti_patterns.name: using batch for multi tool-calling tasks
anti_patterns.explanation: batch api doesnt support multi tool call, use synchronous for agentic workflows

anti_patterns.name: no custom_id on batch requests
anti_patterns.explanation: without it, you cant track the documents, always include meaningful custom id

things_to_know: if someone is waiting for the result - use synchronous
always refine prompt before commiting to large batches
always include custom_id for batch requests
only resubmit only failed batches, not entire batch
batching api doesnt support multi tool calling
batching api is 50% cheaper but has up to 24h latency

anti_patterns.name: using same session to generate and review code
anti_patterns.explanation: code is biased, use new session

anti_patterns.name: running a single pass for 14+ files
anti_patterns.explanation: attention delution and inconsistent depth, split into multi-pass

anti_patterns.name: using extended thinking as a substitute for code review
anti_patterns.explanation: still code is biased, use new session

anti_patterns.name: low confidence (rating) create too many pull request comments
anti_patterns.explanation: use verification pass to reduce noice

anti_patterns.name: skipping cross-pass entirly
anti_patterns.explanation: always include it after local passes

things_to_know: self-review is biased, use separate session for reviews
independed instances per file review catch issues the generator is blind to
multi-pass architecture - per-file parallel instances + cross-file integration (sequential) + confidence verification
cross-file pass - catches data flow issues, api mismatches, inconsistent patterns
confidence rating - routes high-confidence findings to automation, uncertain ones for human reviews
